productRepository: resolved from the current T3 Code checkout

laneSemantics.lane: A named work stream that may contain multiple issues.
laneSemantics.workItem: The delivery state and proof for exactly one issue.
laneSemantics.membership: Every work item names exactly one laneId; an issue cannot appear in two work items.

buildComposition.rule: Every new Test or Dev build is materialized in a new detached worktree at the exact live Theo SwiftUI branch commit. Apply each selected issue's base-to-head patch once, in plan order. A prior combined build may define logical carry membership but is never an ancestor or source base.

evidencePolicy.completion: validate-proof and validate-inspection both pass; generation-plan validation reopens the exact bound artifacts

issueEvidence.purpose: Alex must be able to judge whether a feature is good from its issue ticket alone, without opening the PR, the board, or a worktree.
issueEvidence.rule: Every user-visible work item's GitHub issue embeds the same media its PR will need: full-size before and after screenshots under separate Before and After headings, light and dark appearances, the animated GIF, and the interaction video when the change is motion, scrolling, focus, timing, or gesture-driven - the upstream PR evidence-format bar from CONTRIBUTING_VOUCHED 'Show UI changes in the real app'.
issueEvidence.source: The work item's validated proof is the only media source. Never recapture for the issue, never fabricate, and never commit issue media to the product diff.
issueEvidence.timing: Embed when proof and inspection validate, and refresh the embed whenever proof is replaced. The embed must be current before the item enters a phone-test generation or an open-pr plan.
issueEvidence.format: Upload as GitHub issue attachments so media renders inline - never bare local paths - under headings that name the exact base and head commits and the appearance. Keep the swiftui-work-item-v2 block byte-identical when editing the body.
issueEvidence.exceptions: Non-user-visible work embeds the proof's recorded no-media reason instead of media.

publication.authentication: Use the active gh OAuth bearer token first. The endpoint accepts image and video uploads for a repository the token can push to and returns the final user-attachments URL with HTTP 201.
publication.rule: Validate proof and inspection, publish with the repo-owned tool, preserve the swiftui-work-item-v2 block byte-for-byte, and verify every returned URL from the reread GitHub issue body. Escalate browser or credential authorization only after the tool demonstrates that bearer publication is unavailable for the exact repository or media.

authorizationEscalation.rule: A browser, Computer Use, credential, approval, or other human-authorization dependency is not ordinary waiting. Record it as kind authorization-required, immediately wake the coordinator, and put ACTION REQUIRED FROM ALEX before every normal status section. Name every affected issue, the exact capability or authorization needed, why it is blocked, and what the block prevents. Never hide it in a buffer, parked-work list, or routine progress wording.
authorizationEscalation.legacyCompatibility: Status promotes known legacy GitHub issue-attachment and browser-prohibition waiting reasons to authorization-required so existing gates cannot stay silent.
authorizationEscalation.afterAuthorization: Once Alex authorizes the named action, the coordinator performs or dispatches it immediately within that scope and records a replacement dispatch receipt that clears the stale waiting gate.

backlogDemotion.rule: Alex may return an in-flight item to the backlog without inventing a quality verdict. The transition requires an immutable priority decision receipt bound to the exact issue, source stage, queued destination, decision-maker, authority source, timestamp, and specific reason. Clear derived head/proof/generation/acceptance bindings but retain the launch binding so the old branch remains attributable. Re-entry uses the ordinary queued pull and re-materializes against the current Theo base.
backlogDemotion.notFor: Rejection or rework still returns to active with a verdict; demotion is a scope or priority decision, not a quality verdict.

backlogRestoration.rule: Alex may restore a terminal work item when new product evidence or a later priority decision makes it relevant again. The same exact priority receipt is mandatory. Restore to queued, clear derived implementation and verdict bindings, preserve the prior launch receipt for attribution, then re-materialize from the live Theo base through the ordinary queued pull.

flowPolicy.model: Stations have WIP limits; buffers between stations are unbounded.

sources: Alex's explicit SwiftUI or Electron priorities
SwiftUI defects and desired features observed in the native client
Electron defects and desired features explicitly requested by Alex
backlog.rule: While any approved worker provider has usable token capacity, keep implementation lanes at their WIP limit: dispatch already-ready eligible queued work into open slots first, then replenish only from Alex's SwiftUI and Electron product priorities. A simulator, signing, or phone blocker never idles implementation, test, or review lanes.
backlog.upstreamContributionRule: The upstream contribution queue is discovery and provenance only. Never auto-file, rank, dispatch, or include one of its items in a build. It becomes eligible only after Alex explicitly promotes the concrete behavior as a SwiftUI or Electron product priority.
backlog.reactNativeParityRule: React Native parity is not a backlog source by itself. File or dispatch it only when Alex has asked for that concrete behavior in SwiftUI or Electron and the source behavior still belongs to the current product path.
backlog.paritySourceRule: Before filing parity work, prove the source behavior belongs to the current product path. Do not extend a legacy, deprecated, beta-replaced, or disabled path when a successor path intentionally removed that behavior; target the successor design or do not file the parity item.

bufferStaleness.note: A buffered item pays re-materialization onto the current carry when it advances. Keep items small and file-disjoint so that tax stays low.

accepted.rule: phone-test -> accepted is valid only when the acceptance receipt (schemaVersion 3) binds its successor: a live upstream-handoff dispatch (threadId, thread title carrying #issue, dispatchedAt) created before the verdict is recorded, or an explicit allowed hold that the transition writes into the work item. A bare acceptance cannot exist.

testPublication.standingAuthorization: Alex, 2026-08-26: Test builds for the phone are generated, published, and pushed automatically. As soon as proof-ready work exists that is not in the latest published Test generation, build a new combined Test generation and publish it. No human or agent approval is required for Test generation, publication, or phone installation. Phone ACCEPTANCE verdicts remain Alex's alone.
testPublication.immutableBuilds: Every generation gets its own build directory under buildStore; previous builds are never overwritten or deleted by publication. The ready pointer is replaced atomically only after the new artifact is complete and hash-verified, so the phone always installs the newest complete build even if a newer one is mid-generation.

watcher.label: com.saphid.t3-swiftui-phone-watch
watcher.behavior: Deterministic, no LLM. Every 60s: require a schema-2 pointer that reopens and hashes the generation plan and schema-3 generation receipt, verifies that receipt binds the artifact hash and composed commit, then verify the artifact (sha256, codesign, Info.plist identity), compare installed CFBundleVersion via devicectl, install when the phone is reachable and older, never downgrade, launch, and write a device receipt carrying the generation receipt hash; notify once per build when the phone is locked or absent.

uatThreads.trigger: Every device receipt reporting a newly installed build (status installed*)
uatThreads.name: UAT <build number> (<Test|Dev>) - e.g. 'UAT 78 (Test)'
content: FIRST LINE: which app to open on the phone - 'SwiftUI Test' or 'SwiftUI Dev' (the installed display name) - plus the build number and channel
every included feature/fix: what it is, WHY we need it (from the owning issue's problem statement), and HOW Alex should test it (from the acceptance points, as concrete phone steps)

every entry ties its links to its numbers: the owning issue number with the issue URL, and, when the change came back from an upstream PR, that PR's number with the PR URL - label an unlanded PR as unlanded

every visual change embeds its evidence in the thread itself: full-size dark-mode before and after screenshots under separate headings plus the animated GIF, and a video as well when the change is motion, scrolling, focus, timing, or gesture-driven - the evidence-format bar only, not the PR-time state-capture checklist; never bare local paths
new candidates, pending initial-acceptance carry, reapproval candidates, and accepted unchanged carry listed separately
an explicit accept/reject request only for each new candidate, pending initial-acceptance carry, or reapproval candidate
accepted unchanged installed-carry entries are informational composition context only: identify them as unchanged, request no spot-check, and request no verdict

unchanged installed-carry entries without a prior acceptance receipt remain pending initial acceptance: repeat their original acceptance steps and request a first verdict without calling it a regression or reapproval

for every reapproval candidate, name the exact new head, proof, inspection, replacement, or behavior change; state that prior acceptance does not cover the changed artifact; repeat the current acceptance points as concrete phone steps; and directly ask for reapproval

verdictPolicy.candidate: Requires an explicit accept/reject verdict when the generation introduces behavior that has no acceptance receipt bound to this exact artifact.
verdictPolicy.acceptedRecovery: A one-time migration of behavior Alex already accepted from a historically installed build whose generation receipt is unavailable. It must bind the real verdict source, installed artifact and device receipt, plus the freshly rematerialized overlay; it is informational and requests no new verdict.
verdictPolicy.reapprovalCandidate: A candidate whose previously accepted behavior changed. It must disclose the exact code or behavior change and directly request renewed acceptance.
verdictPolicy.acceptedInstalledCarry: Unchanged composition inherited from the prior installed generation with an acceptance receipt already recorded. It must not trigger a spot-check request, accept/reject request, or renewed acceptance.
verdictPolicy.pendingInstalledCarry: Unchanged composition inherited from the prior installed generation without an acceptance receipt. It still requires its first explicit verdict, using its original acceptance steps and never reapproval language.
verdictPolicy.invariant: Generation role is not human-verdict state. A carry entry never becomes a reapproval request merely because a new Test build includes it; acceptance-receipt state decides whether unchanged carry is accepted context or pending its first verdict, and changed accepted behavior must be represented as a candidate and explained explicitly.

buildReport.issueLinks: Every build-composition entry names its owning issue number and links the issue URL, so any line of the report reaches its issue in one click.
buildReport.upstreamPrLinks: When an entry's change came back from an upstream PR, the entry also names that PR's number and links the PR URL, taken from the work item's recorded upstream references or its landed PR; when the upstream PR is not yet landed, link it too and label it unlanded.
buildReport.visualEvidence: A visual change embeds its evidence in the thread itself, to the upstream PR evidence-format bar (full-size, separate headings, never narrow side-by-side tables) with dark captures only: full-size before and after screenshots under separate headings plus the animated GIF, and a video as well when the change is motion, scrolling, focus, timing, or gesture-driven. The PR-time state-capture checklist is not required in the thread. Simulator proof is unchanged and still records light and dark; only the thread embed is dark-only. Deliver per share-video-evidence: an inline playable attachment or a Tailnet-only URL - never a bare local path.
buildReport.invariant: Alex reads the UAT thread alone to learn what changed, where it came from, and what to check. Any entry that forces opening GitHub, the board, or a worktree to understand the build breaks this contract.

uatThreads.owner: swiftui-orchestrate coordinator duty; verdicts recorded as acceptance receipts
uatThreads.pinned: Pin the thread on creation so it stays at the top of the project. Use the typed client RPC for pinning (probe the websocket RPC contract first per established practice); NEVER write state.sqlite directly. If no typed surface supports pinning, report the gap on the ledger instead.

coordinatorController.boardMembership: infrastructure only; never represented by a delivery work item and never counted in station WIP
coordinatorController.authority: read canonical GitHub, receipt, device, and T3 projections; create or wake one dedicated coordinator thread through T3's typed orchestration API; never transition work items or write GitHub directly
coordinatorController.tokenIndependence: the controller is ordinary Python and always runs without model quota; before dispatch it selects from sanitized provider headroom, creates a new model-bound thread on failover, and records no-model-capacity without dispatch when no candidate safely qualifies
coordinatorController.duplicateProtection: one nonblocking local lock, one live coordinator turn at a time, and a minimum dispatch interval

modelFailover.unknownLaneRule: A candidate with one unreported required lane may run only as a lower-priority probe when every reported required lane is fresh and at least 10% remains. Two unknown required lanes never qualify. Stale is unknown, never available.
modelFailover.selectionRule: Choose the first fully eligible candidate in order. If none is fully eligible, choose the first allowed probe. Exclude a model for 15 minutes after its controller turn errors. A model change or prior controller error always creates a new thread; never rewrite a thread's model.
